video.title: You Can Feel This - Here's How

classification.reason: The coach gives explicit actionable mental cues and movement instructions, directing players to intend to pull the hip back and drive the shoulders forward rather than driving the hip forward.

problem.title_as_question: Why should you feel like pulling your pelvis back when it physically rotates forward?
problem.definition: Players often try to actively drive their right hip forward into the forehand, which paradoxically destroys fascial tension and limits upper body rotation and racket speed.

symptoms.description: The hips and shoulders turn forward together as a single block rather than twisting opposite.
Lack of backward yanking tension felt across the pelvis and external oblique during the forward swing.

causes.statement: The fascial line connecting hip and shoulder creates an equal and opposite tension that flings the shoulder forward while yanking the hip backward.
Consciously trying to send the right hip forward causes the brain to avoid stretching the diagonal tissue line because stretch creates a force resisting hip advancement.
The backward force acts as negative acceleration that decelerates the forward-moving pelvis and hands off energy rather than physically reversing hip position.
Human motor control relies on sensing internal tension and resulting acceleration rather than visual geometric displacement.

angles.summary: Demonstrates the tensioned line between hip and shoulder using a corkscrew model with two anchors.
Demonstrates how bringing the hip forward without shoulder resistance moves further but loses elastic coil.
Clarifies that while the pelvis physically moves forward on video, the internal muscular acceleration is directed backward.

solutions.summary: Think 'drive shoulders forward, pull hips back' instead of trying to push your hip into the shot.

ban_conflict.note: Actively driving the hip forward prevents building elastic fascial tension across the torso.

solutions.summary: Check for the distinct sensation of the pelvis being yanked backwards while the hitting shoulder is yanked forward during the swing.
From your coiled position, initiate the swing by letting the pelvis fire forward first solely to stretch the tissue harder before executing the shoulder forward, hip back snap.
